statement: A* returns a least-cost path whenever the heuristic h is non-negative and satisfies h(goal) = 0, even if h overestimates the remaining cost at some states.
definitions: A*: best-first search over the open list ordered by f(v) = g(v) + h(v) where g is the cost of the path found so far; the search stops and returns the path when a goal node is popped (expanded), not when it is generated. Either tree-search or graph-search (closed set) may be assumed; the counterexample must fail under the chosen convention. Edge costs positive, h non-negative, h(goal) = 0.
